messages:
maria: quick PRD intake — customer ACME wants per-tenant acceptance gates + rollout policy for tenant-specific quality thresholds. Problem: their downstream UX requires deterministic behavior (no surprise rollbacks) when quality dips; they need a clear acceptance criteria set we can test automatically.

maria: goals: 1) define pass/fail acceptance criteria (metric defs + thresholds) 2) propose canary rollout + rollback rules 3) list non-goals (no UI work this phase) 4) delivery plan + success metrics (see below).

maria: non-goals: analytics dashboards, multi-tenant isolation infra changes, or full tenant billing changes.

maria: success metrics: (a) acceptance test run completes in CI for each candidate model, (b) per-tenant quality pass rate >= 96% on customer eval set, (c) end-to-end P95 latency <= 300ms for 95% of tenant requests in canary, (d) infra cost delta <= +20% (target <+10%).

aj: quick q — are quality thresholds absolute or relative to their baseline model? do we need per-tenant baselines or a global baseline?

maria: per-tenant baselines if we can get historical logs; otherwise fall back to global baseline with tenant-specific overrides later.

neha: for the acceptance criteria I suggest two tiers: (1) automated eval harness pass (precision/recall or whatever metric customer uses) + no regression > 1% vs baseline, (2) live canary monitoring for semantic drift with manual review triggers. Need sample eval prompts from ACME.

aj: also callout: caching + prefix KV will skew latency numbers. we should specify sequence length distribution for the canary to make P95 meaningful.

sanjay: from infra side — clarify SLA expectations for Dedicated vs Hosted routing during rollout. If we route to Dedicated and fallback to Hosted, what are SLOs?

maria: proposed routing policy: prefer Dedicated for canary; fallback to Hosted only on capacity/health issues. Rollback if customer quality metric drops > 2% absolute or if error rate > 0.5% for 5m.

neha: edge cases to call out: extremely long inputs (>8k tokens), malformed/ binary payloads, and tenant-level adversarial prompts. These should be non-goal mitigations (reject + instrument) for phase 1.

aj: for acceptance tests can we require a deterministic output comparator? i.e., structured evaluation harness so we can run CI diffs and flag regressions automatically.

maria: yes — require harness + example golden outputs. I'll share ACME eval set link in a follow-up.

product-bot: RFC template: https://redwood-internal/rfcs/template — use the "canary-rollout-acceptance" section.

sanjay: cost question — infra can absorb up to +20% temporarily, but we should aim for <+10% for production commit. Confirming that as a requirement helps ops.

maria: confirmed — committed target <+10%, hard cap +20% for short trial.

aj: small implementation note: quantized model variants may affect quality metrics — we should include model variant matrix in the RFC (float16, q4, q8).

neha: will add test cases for long-tail prompts and a small adversarial set.

maria: plan: aj will draft RFC this week with acceptance criteria + rollout steps; neha will attach eval harness plan; sanjay will note routing/SLOs + cost constraints. After draft, we'll do a 1hr review with ACME SREs.

aj: sounds good, I'll put a draft up by Thu. @maria please add the sample eval set. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: RFC draft created: #234 — draft: "tenant-acceptance-gates-v1" (reviewers: maria, aj, neha, sanjay)

maria: thanks all — moving this to RFC stage. will add timeline and owner in the doc.

aj: ack.

neha: ack.

sanjay: ack.
